flagged.evidence: Step 7.1 derives a pointwise bound `limsup_j v_j(w) <= -log r_2` and then says 'Upper semicontinuity and compactness of \overline\Delta_\sigma therefore give J such that ...'. But [L6] only says that subharmonic means 'upper semicontinuous together with the disc submean inequality', and [L7] only says plane subharmonic functions are locally integrable so Fatou applies to disc averages. Those inputs do not license an eventual uniform-on-compact bound from a pointwise limsup bound. Counterexample to the cited inference pattern: on the compact interval [0,1], let v_j(x)=1 at x=1/j and 0 elsewhere. Each v_j is upper semicontinuous, and pointwise limsup_j v_j(x)=0 for every x, yet no J makes v_j<=1/2 on all of [0,1] for every j>=J. The uniform tail estimate needed for step 8.1 is therefore unsupported.

Step 1.2 says that extending each fixed-parameter two-variable slice by [L1] 'produces a function on the whole polydisc that is separately holomorphic and locally bounded'. The cited dependency [L1], [[thm-hartogs-figure-extension]], states only: 'Every holomorphic function on the Hartogs figure H(r,s) admits a unique holomorphic extension to the bidisc \widehat H(r,s).' Applied slicewise, that yields an extension for each fixed passive parameter, but it does not show that the assembled function is holomorphic in the passive coordinates, or even separately holomorphic there. The key assembled-function claim is asserted without a licensing dependency.

Step 2.1 says 'Applying [L2] gives a holomorphic extension of f from G to G\cup P_1\cup\cdots\cup P_N.' But [L2] is [[lem-propagation-and-gluing-of-hartogs-extensions]], whose statement assumes only `U_j\cap(G\cup U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_{j-1})\cap G\ne\varnothing`, and whose step 2.1 concludes that the new local extension and the previously glued function 'agree on every connected overlap component'. That hypothesis guarantees only that the overlap meets G somewhere; it does not ensure that every connected overlap component meets a nonempty open subset of G, so the cited gluing lemma does not establish the extension claimed here.

The page says: 'Separate holomorphy is converted into joint holomorphy through the Baire-plus-local-boundedness argument, then Hartogs figures are propagated across shell neighborhoods and glued along overlaps. The final extension theorem records the finite shell-cover form of the compact hole argument ...' On current disk, the local-boundedness route still has the unsupported uniformization step flagged above in [[lem-local-boundedness-of-separately-holomorphic-functions]] 7.1, the shell-propagation route still has the unsupported assembled-function step in [[lem-local-hartogs-extension-across-polydisc-shells]] 1.2, and the compact-hole theorem [[thm-hartogs-extension-across-compact-holes]] still relies on the weak gluing lemma just described. So the prose states that these routes are established even though the current proofs do not support them.
